name: NIH Kirschstein-NRSA Individual Predoctoral Fellowship (F31)
what: The [F31](#term:f-award) supports a doctoral student who carries out mentored research training in a health-related field under a faculty sponsor [736](#cite:736). It is one of the Ruth L. The award pays a stipend, a contribution to tuition and fees and an [institutional allowance](#term:institutional-allowance); NIH sets the amounts for each fiscal year in a notice [736](#cite:736) [732](#cite:732).

who_may_apply.investigator: The candidate is currently enrolled in a PhD or equivalent research degree programme (for example EngD, DNSc, DrPH, DSW, PharmD, ScD) and names a sponsor who will supervise the training [736](#cite:736).
who_may_apply.limits: The notice sets no cap on applications per organization; NIH does not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time [736](#cite:736). NIH's limit of six applications per [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) per calendar year applies to all [activity codes](#term:activity-code) except T codes and R13 conference [grants](#term:grant); the notice names no exception for F or K codes [12](#cite:12).

steps: The [applicant organization](#term:applicant-organization) holds registrations in [SAM](#term:sam-gov) (which issues the [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei)), [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) and [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov); the candidate needs an eRA Commons account linked to an [ORCID iD](#term:orcid) [784](#cite:784).

The organization submits the application to Grants.gov through [NIH ASSIST](#term:nih-assist), an institutional system-to-system solution or [Grants.gov Workspace](#term:grants-gov-workspace); referees send reference letters through eRA Commons, not Grants.gov [784](#cite:784).
The student identifies a sponsor, who commits to the training plan and to direct supervision of the research [736](#cite:736).
Referees submit reference letters; an application without the required letters is not reviewed [736](#cite:736).
The application is due on April 08, August 08 or December 08 [736](#cite:736).
Training abroad needs a detailed justification and is funded only when the scientific advantages are clear [736](#cite:736).
owner: National Institutes of Health (HHS)
eligibility_note: Eligible applicant organizations include nonprofits other than [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), with or without [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status, as well as federal agencies and foreign organizations; the organization must have staff and facilities on site for the training [736](#cite:736). citizenship: By the time of award the candidate must be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States, or lawfully admitted for permanent residence [736](#cite:736) [757](#cite:757).
career_window: Students currently enrolled in a research doctoral programme. An individual may receive up to 5 years of aggregate NRSA support at the predoctoral level, or up to 6 years for dual-degree training [736](#cite:736).
stipend: $29,364 a year ($2,447 a month) for predoctoral fellows on awards made with FY 2026 funds [732](#cite:732). The FY 2025 level was $28,788 [733](#cite:733).
obligation: The [payback obligation](#term:service-obligation) attaches to the first 12 months of postdoctoral NRSA support; the notice and the policy statement as read state no service obligation for predoctoral support [737](#cite:737) [769](#cite:769).

name: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)
what: GRFP gives a graduate student three years of support, to be used within a five-year fellowship period, for a research-based master's or doctoral degree in a STEM field [818](#cite:818) [817](#cite:817). The student applies directly to NSF; the money is then awarded to the university where the fellow enrols, which pays the [stipend](#term:stipend) and receives a [cost-of-education allowance](#term:institutional-allowance) [818](#cite:818). The [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) for the FY 2027 competition is NSF 26-526, posted August 25, 2026 [817](#cite:817).

who_may_apply.investigator: Two levels may apply [818](#cite:818). Level 1 is undergraduates in the final year of a bachelor's degree, and bachelor's degree holders who have never enrolled in a graduate degree programme [818](#cite:818). Level 2 is joint bachelor's-master's students in the final undergraduate or first graduate year, and first-year graduate students in their first graduate programme with less than one academic year completed [818](#cite:818) [820](#cite:820). Second-year graduate students are not eligible [818](#cite:818). All graduate enrolment counts, whatever the field [821](#cite:821).
who_may_apply.limits: One application per annual competition [818](#cite:818). Undergraduate seniors and bachelor's degree holders with no graduate enrolment may apply any number of times before enrolling; a graduate student may apply only once, in the first year of the first graduate programme [818](#cite:818).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: Fellows must enrol in an accredited non-profit graduate degree-granting [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) with a campus in the United States, its territories or possessions, or Puerto Rico [818](#cite:818). A non-profit that is not a degree-granting institution cannot be the fellow's institution [818](#cite:818). Professional and practice-oriented degree programmes, including MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM and DDS, are excluded, as are listed areas of study and kinds of proposed research tied to health, clinical practice, and policy or management implementation [818](#cite:818) [820](#cite:820).

steps: The applicant checks academic level, degree programme, field of study and proposed research against Section IV of the solicitation; an application that fails any of these may be returned without review [818](#cite:818) [861](#cite:861).

The applicant opens a [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) account and prepares the application in the GRFP module of Research.gov; nothing sent another way is accepted [887](#cite:887) [818](#cite:818).

The application holds two statements, each with headings for [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit): a Personal, Relevant Background and Future Goals Statement of at most three pages and a Graduate Research Plan Statement of at most two pages [887](#cite:887).

The applicant names at least three reference writers and may name up to five; at least two letters must reach NSF through the reference letter system by the reference deadline, and the top three are considered [818](#cite:818) [887](#cite:887).
Official undergraduate transcripts are required; a graduate transcript may be unofficial where the institution issues no official one for the first term [818](#cite:818).
A fellow who accepts enrols at an eligible institution, which administers the award; the fellowship can be transferred to another institution after the first fellowship year [818](#cite:818).
